business_summary: e.l.f. Beauty operates in cosmetics. The evidence shows revenue growing at a 41.4% three-year CAGR to FY26, with an operating margin of 9.35% and FY26 net profit of 26.32 USD m. No company documents were supplied, so this description of the business is limited.
why_own: The case rests on very fast sales growth (41.4% three-year CAGR) that has so far come with thinner profitability: net profit growth was -24.65% a year over three years and operating margin fell 5.46 pp. Evidence is thin because no results or call documents were supplied and there is no own-history P/E comparison, so the drivers below are metric-only and the cause of the margin and profit trend is untested.

drivers.statement: Sales keep compounding at a high rate: three-year revenue CAGR stays well above 25%, against 41.4% now. (warn line tightened by code from 25 to 28.98.)
Operating margin stabilises rather than eroding further; it is 9.35% after falling 5.46 pp over three years.
Leverage stays moderate: debt/equity is 0.74x and should not climb materially while profit is thin. (warn line tightened by code from 1 to 0.96.)
Return on equity should stay above 10%. (added by code: currently 2.78.)
Trailing P/E should stay below 60x, or the price needs years of flawless growth. (added by code: currently 113.59.)

kill_criteria.description: Operating margin falls below 5%, meaning growth is no longer converting into adequate profit.
Three-year revenue CAGR drops below 10%, which would remove the growth the thesis is built on.

risks.statement: Profit has not kept up with sales. Three-year net profit CAGR is -24.65%, FY26 net profit is 26.32 USD m, and one of the last four quarters was loss-making. The reasons are untested here.

Valuation is demanding relative to current earnings and book value: trailing P/E is 113.59x and price/book is 5.99x, while ROCE is 2.05% and ROE is 2.78%. There is no own-history P/E comparison to judge it against.
Borrowings are 0.74x equity while returns on capital are low, so there is limited cushion if profit weakens further.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis is wrong if growth is being bought with profit and the market is paying for the growth alone. Revenue has compounded at 41.4% while net profit fell 24.65% a year and operating margin fell 5.46 pp. ROE is 2.78% and ROCE 2.05%, so new sales are earning very little on capital. At a 113.59x trailing P/E, only a sharp margin recovery justifies the price. The thesis fails if margin keeps sliding toward the lenient lines (K1 at 5%, D2 break at 6%) or growth slows, while borrowings of 0.74x equity leave little cushion. Nothing supplied explains why margin fell. What would change this view: Two or more consecutive reported periods of operating margin rising above about 10% with net profit growing and ROE moving toward 10%, or company disclosures showing the margin decline was temporary and one-off.
